table.name: Documents
table.purpose: Master list of documents (articles, CVs, reviews, etc.), each linked to a layout template and containing paragraphs stored in the Paragraphs table.

Document_Description.name: Document_Description
Document_Description.description: Short description or category code of the document. Values are single letters (y, h, w, b, f, r, k, z, n) with no evident meaning; the specific letter-to-meaning mapping is unknown. Could also be a status/type flag, but no joined evidence distinguishes these readings.

Document_ID.name: Document_ID
Document_ID.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each document. Referenced by Paragraphs.Document_ID, which stores the document's paragraph content.

Document_Name.name: Document_Name
Document_Name.description: Human-readable title of the document (e.g. 'A history of Arts', 'Robbin CV', 'Customer reviews'). Unique per row.

Template_ID.name: Template_ID
Template_ID.description: Foreign key to Templates.Template_ID, indicating which template/layout the document uses. The lookup table's Template_Details labels are empty, so the meaning of individual template IDs is unknown.

table.name: Paragraphs
table.purpose: Stores individual paragraphs extracted from documents; each row is one paragraph belonging to a document. In this sample the paragraph text values are country names, suggesting the documents are country-related (e.g., country profiles or reports) and paragraphs are short entries like country names.

Document_ID.name: Document_ID
Document_ID.description: Identifier of the document this paragraph belongs to; references Documents.Document_ID (many paragraphs per document).

Paragraph_ID.name: Paragraph_ID
Paragraph_ID.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the paragraph.

Paragraph_Text.name: Paragraph_Text
Paragraph_Text.description: Text content of the paragraph. In this data all values are country names (e.g., Korea, Brazil, Fiji, Japan), so paragraphs here appear to be short country-name entries rather than prose.

table.name: Ref_Template_Types
table.purpose: Lookup/reference table of template type categories. Each row is a distinct document template type (code + description) referenced by the Templates table.

Template_Type_Code.name: Template_Type_Code
Template_Type_Code.description: Short code identifying a template type (primary key). Values: AD=Advertisement, BK=Book, CV=CV, PP=Paper, PPT=Presentation. Referenced by Templates.Template_Type_Code.

Template_Type_Description.name: Template_Type_Description
Template_Type_Description.description: Human-readable label of the template type (e.g. Advertisement, Book, CV, Paper, Presentation).

table.name: Templates
table.purpose: Catalog of document templates, each with a type (presentation, CV, advertisement, paper, book), a version number, and an effective validity period. Templates are referenced by Documents, which presumably instantiate them; Paragraphs likely hold template content. The data appears synthetic/test data (empty details, From dates after To dates), so the effective-date semantics are nominal rather than reliable.

Date_Effective_From.name: Date_Effective_From
Date_Effective_From.description: Start of the template's validity/effective period, stored as text but parseable as a datetime. Note: in several rows it is later than Date_Effective_To, so the data does not consistently honor interval semantics.

Date_Effective_To.name: Date_Effective_To
Date_Effective_To.description: End of the template's validity/effective period, stored as text but parseable as a datetime. Often earlier than the From date in this data, so the interval meaning is nominal.

Template_ID.name: Template_ID
Template_ID.description: Primary key of the Templates table; unique integer identifier for each template. Referenced by Documents.Template_ID, linking documents to the template they were created from.

Template_Type_Code.name: Template_Type_Code
Template_Type_Code.description: Code identifying the template's type; foreign key to Ref_Template_Types. Values: PPT=Presentation, CV=CV, AD=Advertisement, PP=Paper, BK=Book.

Version_Number.name: Version_Number
Version_Number.description: Version of the template, an integer 0-9; multiple templates share the same version number, so it distinguishes revisions within a template type rather than being unique. Alternatively it could be part of a composite key with Template_ID, but the data does not confirm this.
